institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Learning the language (french) was a central reason to choose Paris as a destination. Also the academic opportunities at Sciences Po attracted me. Finally I really wanted to explore french culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, I generally experienced that the staff at Sciences Po were helpful / available via e-mail to answer questions when you contacted them

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was several offers of introductory tours, guides etc, but I did not make use of them as I did not find it neccesary

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing via Fondation Danoise in the Cité Universitaire. It was an amazing experience staying in Fondation Danoise, and applying is very much recommended. Since I was lucky to get offered a room there, I however don't have a great idea off how difficult it would have been to find other types of housing off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For living in Cité Universitaire particularly, I had a really great experience, however it should be noted that I think experiences can vary a lot depending on what house you end up in / if you get exchanged to a different house. In general the Cité is a really unique place, and I loved staying there, but it is of course a more international environment where it is more likely that you will encounter people from your home country as well as people from all over the world, than many locals. For a more "local" experience, other types of housing might be preferred. However, I personally have nothing bad to say about living in Fondation Danoise, to me it was a great experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Overall I found it fine, however be aware in the registration period to check your host institution platforms (both e-mail and other platforms) regularly so you don't miss any new added requirements and deadlines

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online resources were available as I recall it, and also I found that you could get questions answered via e-mail if necessary.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was luckily a 100% succesfull, however the course registration process is very stressfull and I know of several people who did not get the classes that they had gotten pre-approved. However, I dont know of any for whom it did not work out in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When it comes to course registration I would advice you to get as many course as possible pre-approved as course registration is very competitive and course get filled up in a matter of seconds. Also make a structured plan of what courses you need to apply to, and be ready on the clock when registration opens. Also have a list of relevant alternatives ready (even if you did not get them pre-approved yet). Finally if you did not get you courses, keep refreshing and revisiting the page over the registration period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally I did not find the level of the course in terms of theory and complexity to match the level of my home university, neither did I find the academic standards for assignments very high. With that said the courses where in no way easy, a really large workload was required as well as generally a good deal of factual knowledge (even in introduction level classes) if you wanted to perform well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The approach is way more practical than theoretical, which I enjoyed in most parts. Linked to this it was rewarding to be thought by professionals from a given field. Furthermore, the style of teaching is based on mandatory participation and several assignments, presentations etc in each course that are mandatory and part of your grade, thus I found that you did not have much autonomy to manage your own time which I did not really enjoy. Lastly, teaching was often not very closely linked to the readings. Finally, some teachers had a more "old school" way of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Politics - ASPO 25A11

European integration and it's challenges - DSPO 25A02 


The Decision-Making Process of the  European Union: An insiders view - DSPO 25A13

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Decision-Making Process of the  European Union: An insiders view - DSPO 25A13 

This was the only course that I really enjoyed. The courses was thought in a more "old school" style, with the teacher mainly speaking and drawing a lot on personal experience, however I found this really rewarding and I learned so much about the European Union and how it worked from this class. The prof is really nice, and it was just such a nice and rewarding experience following his class.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *

The academic work load is a lot be prepared for that 

Do yourself the favor of engaging in learning some french while you are there or beforehand if you have time, it is not necessary at all but will make it easier to talk to locals and it is just a good opportunity
